name: Haimabati Dey
title: Electrical and Computer Engineer
tagline: Analog and mixed-signal circuits · CMOS · Spintronics · Nanophotonics
bio: Electrical and computer engineer with research and engineering experience in analog/mixed-signal circuits, CMOS and device modeling, high-speed communication, RF systems, optical communication, and hardware prototyping.

Research experience includes nano-bio-photonic, plasmonic, and metamaterial structures; quantum optical systems; and spintronic/nanoelectronic devices. Current research interests include physics-aware inverse design and learning methods for magnonics, spin-wave dynamics, nonlinear magnetic systems, and unconventional computing.

research_interests.title: Nano-bio-optoelectronic interfaces
research_interests.text: Investigating optoelectronic device geometries for biological sensing at tissue level, including physical modelling and electrical characterization.

research_interests.title: Integrated CMOS–MTJ structures
research_interests.text: Device and circuit design involving Landau–Lifshitz–Gilbert dynamics, micromagnetic and spin-wave models, nonlinear spin-wave dynamics, magnon interactions, and engineered spin-wave propagation.

research_interests.title: 2D spintronics and magnonics
research_interests.text: Design of spintronic and magnonic structures for logic and sensing-based information processing.

research_interests.title: Wireless nanoscale biosensors
research_interests.text: Compact sensor architectures combining nanoscale transduction, low-power electronics, and wireless signal transmission for biological monitoring.

research_interests.title: RF and integrated circuits for neurotechnology
research_interests.text: Low-noise sensing, energy-efficient wireless readout, miniaturized RF interfaces, and integrated electronics for neural interfaces.

research_interests.title: Intelligent biocompatible nanophotonic and nanoelectronic systems
research_interests.text: Physics-informed machine learning and computational methods for sensor design, biological signal interpretation, and adaptive smart-sensing architectures.
